transcript: 00:00 Maya Patel: okay, uh good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 45 minutes, we want to run through onboarding status and the perf results from last week, quick check on access and then next steps 00:14 Lina Gomez: thanks Maya, yeah, hey all, Lina here, we got the sample dataset uploaded per the instructions, there was one mapping issue with patient_id fields but Tom fixed with a schema transform 00:29 Tom Chen: yeah, the schema mapping, so we mapped patient_id -> pid, there was a couple of nulls, but otherwise upload went fine, storage is in our sandbox s3 bucket 00:42 Ethan Price: cool, thanks Tom, quick note from the perf run we did internally: with the default 8k context we saw tail latency around 180 to 220 ms per token for the quantized variant, un-quantized was 110 to 130 ms, throughput about 28 tokens/s on a single gpuslice 01:05 Marcus Li: when you say gpuslice do you mean the dedicated instance or shared hosted? 01:10 Ethan Price: yeah good q, that was on a dedicated Redwood GPU pool with 1/4 vGPU slice; latency numbers are influenced by batching and our KV cache hit rate, which was about 72% in that run 01:25 Priya Rao: sorry can you spell KV cache? I heard KV cash on the doc earlier, we need clear docs on cache eviction and what is stored 01:33 Ethan Price: absolutely, KV cache, key-value cache sorry transcription hiccup, it's the model kv cache for autoregressive context, we will include a short doc on eviction policy and what stays in memory 01:46 Maya Patel: on access — Tom, you were going to set up a service account and do the VPC peering request? 01:52 Tom Chen: correct, I started the ticket yesterday, but blocked on the CIDR ranges from Redwood, I don't have the test CIDR to put in the peering request yet 02:02 Maya Patel: I'll attach the recommended test CIDR in the email after this call, it's 10.100.0.0/24 for the test cluster, that should be ephemeral, ok? 02:12 Tom Chen: perfect, that'll unblock next step 02:15 Lina Gomez: quick question about encryption, we need to know if Redwood can use our KMS or if we must use Redwood-managed keys 02:24 Maya Patel: short answer: we support both; for Private deployments customers can bring their own KMS via our KMS integration and HSM connectors, for hosted POC we can set up customer-managed keys in AWS KMS, we'll share the flow 02:36 Priya Rao: please add diagram, and how audit logs are surfaced to customer — we need to provide this to compliance 02:42 Maya Patel: yes, I'll share the SOC2 + KMS flow and audit log example, note that audit logs are pushed to customer S3 or via SIEM hooks 02:52 Lina Gomez: great, thanks 02:55 Ethan Price: on the perf side, couple of follow-ups — the 72% KV hit was because we had limited prefix caching, when we turned on prefix caching aggressively the effective latency dropped to 95 to 120 ms for the quantized path but with higher token cost due to less batching 03:16 Marcus Li: can you explain token cost tradeoff again? 03:20 Ethan Price: yep, basically batching reduces per-token cost because you amortize compute, but aggressive prefix caching reduces recomputation by reusing KV state which lowers latency but increases cache memory and sometimes reduces batchability — it's a knobs tradeoff 03:35 Tom Chen: for our use case we need sub-150ms 95th percentile for chat UI, is that realistic on the quantized model? 03:44 Ethan Price: probably yes with pinned dedicated capacity and prefix caching enabled; also quantization profile matters — we had a good model-quant profile for the benchmark but we can run a targeted run with your exact prompt mix to validate 03:58 Lina Gomez: what about data residency? our legal says some PHI-derived data must stay in-region for EU users 04:05 Maya Patel: noted, we have region pinning for both hosted and private; for the POC we can run the benchmark in eu-west-1 if you provide the sample subset from EU region, otherwise Private deployment solves residency as well 04:20 Priya Rao: also SSO, we need SAML SSO to be enabled for seats on the console 04:26 Samira Khan: (CSM) we can support SAML integration, we'll send the SAML metadata template, need a customer admin to accept 04:33 Tom Chen: quick infra question, does Redwood require any inbound firewall ports for the peering or is it all egress? 04:40 Ethan Price: peering is layer 3, typically egress from your side to our endpoints, no inbound open ports required but we'll share the exact port list, and for private/on-prem there are additional firewall needs 04:53 Lina Gomez: ok cool, thanks, another small thing on the dataset we saw a couple of name tokenization errors in the prompt parsing, maybe punctuation or titles cause truncation 05:03 Ethan Price: yep those are tokenization issues, likely due to punctuation splitting in the preprocessing step, we can provide a sanitize script and also suggest turning off aggressive truncation for certain fields 05:16 Tom Chen: action — we'll try the sanitize script once you send it, that's on our side 05:20 Maya Patel: noted 05:22 Ethan Price: for the benchmark we'll run a 1-hour steady-state run with 2 concurrent clients reproducing your UI pattern, we'll capture p95/p99 and memory KPIs, then we'll post logs to the shared folder 05:37 Lina Gomez: perfect, and then after that we expect a summary slide deck with recommendations on batching/caching/quant settings so we can decide on Dedicated vs Hosted 05:48 Maya Patel: yes we'll provide a decision matrix based on latency vs cost for the options we test 05:55 Priya Rao: any concerns about PHI in logs? we need assurances that logs are either redacted or stored in our controlled bucket 06:03 Ethan Price: logs from the perf run will be redacted of PHI by default and we can push raw logs to your S3 if you prefer under your KMS key 06:12 Marcus Li: timeline question: what's the earliest we can have a pilot go-live assuming POC results are good? 06:20 Maya Patel: typically 2-3 weeks after POC depending on security sign-offs and infra availability, Dedicated ramps longer if you need reserved capacity 06:33 Tom Chen: ok, for resource planning we'll assume 3 weeks, that works 06:36 Lina Gomez: are there any licensing or egress fees we should budget for? 06:41 Maya Patel: POC is covered under the eval agreement, for production you'd see usage-based pricing and Reserved if you choose Dedicated — we'll share a rough estimate after the perf run 06:53 Priya Rao: minor thing, can you confirm retention period for audit logs and how easy it is to export to our SIEM? 06:59 Maya Patel: audit logs retention is configurable; default 90 days, we can push to your SIEM via webhook or S3; we'll include the exact steps in the security pack 07:10 Ethan Price: one more perf note — if we see 95th percentile spikes, we'll try two levers: increase prefix cache hit rate and lower batch windows; both reduce spikes but affect cost differently 07:24 Tom Chen: let's make sure the cost delta is visible in the report so we can estimate monthly spend 07:29 Maya Patel: yep decision matrix will include token/unit cost and latency impact 07:35 Lina Gomez: ok shall we recap next steps? 07:37 Maya Patel: recap — Redwood sends SOC2/KMS/audit docs (Maya) by tomorrow, Redwood runs 1-hour perf with our sample and posts logs (Ethan) by Mon 6/28, Tom to create service account and approve VPC peering (Tom) by Sun 6/27, Priya to compile compliance Qs (Priya) by 7/1 07:57 Samira Khan: I'll follow up to schedule the quantization deep-dive if needed 08:02 Lina Gomez: thanks everyone, appreciate the progress 08:05 Maya Patel: thanks all, end call
